reproduction_target: Computational metagenomic analysis of gut-microbiome CAZyme pool and SCFA-production capacity across three Argentine cohorts (reference, average, IBD): low-pass metagenome functional annotation with SqueezeMeta, CAZyme identification with dbCAN3, SCFA-enzyme assignment via 42 KEGG identifiers (FPM normalization), and statistical/visual analysis with scipy + matplotlib. Wet-lab fecal processing, IgG MACS sorting, and NextSeq 550 sequencing are out of computational-reproduction scope (counted in W).
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool from Methods prose of the bioRxiv v2 PDF (biorxiv HTML/JATS were Cloudflare 403/429-blocked; PDF fetched from the cloudfront full.pdf mirror, abstract cross-checked against Europe PMC PPR1022515). Author code repo github.com/militrot/cazymes contains only two analysis Jupyter notebooks (Cazymes_analysis.ipynb, Cazymes_analysis_version2.ipynb) + a prose README; README describes no environment (no conda/lockfile/Docker/pinned versions). Notebooks not read at line level (stage1). No named tool carries a version pin anywhere in the prose.

steps.label: SqueezeMeta metagenomic annotation pipeline (functional/taxonomic profiling of low-pass reads, ~1.3M reads/sample) — no version, no invocation script in repo
dbCAN3 CAZyme (carbohydrate-active enzyme) identification/annotation — no version, no invocation script in repo
SCFA-enzyme assignment via 42 KEGG identifiers with FPM (fragments-per-million) normalization — KEGG release not pinned, the 42-ID list not enumerated in prose
scipy statistical analysis (parametric/non-parametric test selection by homoscedasticity, p-value thresholds)
matplotlib visualization of CAZyme diversity/abundance and SCFA capacity (boxplots, PCoA plots)
